'''Krikor Peshtimaldjian''' ({{langx|hy|Գրիգոր Փեշտիմալջյան}}, Born [[Constantinople]], [[Ottoman Turkey]] 1778 - died [[Constantinople]], [[Ottoman Turkey]] January, 1839) was an ethnic [[Armenian people|Armenian]] philosopher, educator, translator, and linguist.<ref name="The Heritage of Armenian Literature From The Eighteenth Century To Modern Times.">{{cite book|last=J. Hacikyan|first=Agop|title=The Heritage of Armenian Literature From The Eighteenth Century To Modern Times.|year=2005|publisher=Wayne State Univ Pr|location=Detroit|isbn=9780814332214|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GmtPLvnrc38C&q=Peshtimaldjian&pg=PA189|access-date=27 February 2021|pages=189–190}}</ref> He was a key figure in the [[Armenian national awakening]] and reformist movement in the 19th century.<ref>{{cite book|last=Arpee|first=Leon|title=The Armenian awakening: a history of the Armenian church, 1820-1860|year=1909|publisher=University of Chicago Press|location=Chicago|url=https://archive.org/details/armenianawakeni00arpegoog}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Leon|first=Arpee|title=A century of Armenian Protestantism, 1846-1946|year=1946|publisher=The Armenian missionary association of America, inc|pages=96}}</ref>
